Quasem took Ranjit Das to torture camp in 1971
2014-02-19T00:00:24+06:00 | Staff Correspondent
https://www.thedailystar.net/quasem-took-ranjit-das-to-torture-camp-in-1971-12021

A prosecution witness yesterday told International Crimes Tribunal-2 that he learnt from his mother that Al-Badr men led by Jamaat-e-Islami leader Mir Quasem Ali took his father, Ranjit Das, to the Dalim Hotel torture camp during the Liberation War. His father was tortured to death at the hotel in Chittagong city along with their neighbour Tuntu Sen, said Shibu Das, 46, quoting his mother. He testified as the fifth prosecution witness (PW) at the three-member tribunal headed by Justice Obaidul Hassan. Ranjit ran a teashop and a business of old bottles. Shibu, who works at a metal workshop, said he was about three years old when his father was killed and could not even remember the face of his father. In his short deposition, he also said Dalim Hotel was a den of Al-Badr in 1971 where many innocent people were tortured and killed. Al-Badr, notorious auxiliary force to the Pakistani army, looted valuables of Hindus and torched their houses. Following the testimony, defence counsel Mizanul Islam completed cross-examining the witness. The defence also completed cross-examining the fourth prosecution witness, Sunil Kanti Bardhan, who testified Monday against Quasem. The proceeding was adjourned until today. Meanwhile, Quasem's son and counsel Barrister Mir Ahmad Binquasemson filed an application seeking a "suitable" vehicle for the transportation of his father, citing his health condition. The tribunal is due to pass an order regarding this on February 20.

Quasem is facing 14 charges of crimes against humanity he allegedly committed during the Liberation War.
